name: Finance
hook: Students build the model in ten minutes, so the class time goes to arguing about the assumptions.

make.body: Physical decision cards or a data object for a simulation: a term structure or a risk distribution rendered as something you can hold and compare side by side. Useful precisely because it slows the reading down.

build.body: A working interactive model for a real decision, built live. The assignment is not the model. It is the sensitivity analysis and the written defense of every assumption the model needed to make.

plan.txt: Pick a real decision with public filings. Students list every assumption required, before building anything.
Build the interactive model with AI in class. Break it deliberately: what input makes the conclusion flip?
Sensitivity write-up plus fabrication of the physical comparison cards.
Defense session. Another team’s job is to find the assumption that carries the whole result.

prompt: Build a single self-contained HTML page with an interactive model for this decision: [describe the decision]. Include sliders for every input that matters. Show the output updating live, and display the break-even point prominently. Then list every assumption you had to make to build it, and tell me which single assumption the conclusion is most sensitive to.
tryTuesday: 90 minutes, one real decision with public numbers. Minutes 0–20: students list every assumption a model of the decision would require, before building anything. Minutes 20–55: they build the interactive model with the prompt (or open the embedded break-even demo) and deliberately break it — find the single input that flips the conclusion. Minutes 55–90: teams trade models and each hunts the assumption that carries the whole result. The deliverable is the sensitivity finding: which assumption the answer is most fragile to, with the evidence. It grades reasoning about assumptions, not model-building.

replaces.assignment: The valuation or capital-budgeting spreadsheet submitted as the answer.
replaces.lost: The hand-built modeling mechanics and formula fluency.
replaces.gained: With AI building the model in minutes, class time moves to the actual professional skill — defending assumptions and finding the one the conclusion hinges on — instead of grading spreadsheet arithmetic a tool now does.

aiFailsHere: A model builds a financial model that runs cleanly and hides its load-bearing assumptions — silently setting overhead to zero, assuming no ramp-up, holding margins constant, and presenting a confident break-even without surfacing that one uncertain input drives the result. Its output looks decision-ready while burying exactly the assumptions a sensitivity analysis is supposed to expose.

rubric.description: The student surfaces the assumptions the model required, including the ones the AI set silently.
Correctly identifies the single assumption the conclusion is most fragile to, with evidence from varying it.
Finds the input that flips the conclusion and explains why.
Defends the assumptions that hold and concedes the one that does not when another team attacks the model.

budget.perStudentCost: $0 for the Tuesday version; roughly $8–15 per team in laser stock for engraved decision and comparison cards in the four-week build.
budget.fileDueWeek: Week 3 — cut file due with the sensitivity write-up.
budget.calendarNote: Model-building needs no lead time; the physical comparison cards depend on the 7–10 day cut turnaround.

scales.oneSession: The 90-minute build-break-and-trade session producing a sensitivity finding; no fabrication.
scales.fourWeeks: The seeded four-week plan: assumption list, AI model broken deliberately, sensitivity write-up plus fabricated cards, then a defense session.
scales.oneSemester: A full decision case with public filings — assumption inventory, an AI-built model stress-tested repeatedly, fabricated comparison cards, and a defense session where another team must find the assumption carrying the result.

promptOutput.model: Claude (Anthropic) — captured 2026-07-27 in an isolated fresh session with no build context; output is unedited.
promptOutput.promptFilled: Filled in as a Honolulu food-truck owner deciding whether to sign a three-year Chinatown brick-and-mortar lease, with sliders for rent, average ticket, daily covers, food-cost percentage, and wages.

annotations.marker: Self-listed six assumptions, including 'all other overhead... set to zero'
annotations.note: The model surfaced its own load-bearing simplifications — the assumption inventory the assignment demands, done unprompted.

annotations.marker: Named the most sensitive assumption: daily covers
annotations.note: Correctly reasoned that covers multiplies both revenue and cost deduction and is least certain — the sensitivity insight the exercise grades.

annotations.marker: Zeroed overhead silently in the formula, then admitted it
annotations.note: The break-even is contribution-based and omits utilities, insurance, permits, and build-out; a student trusting the headline number without reading the note would be badly misled.

annotations.marker: Ignored the lease's own terms (deposit, escalators, three-year commitment)
annotations.note: It flagged that the multi-year commitment 'carries no modeled cost beyond monthly rent' — a real omission for a decision that is fundamentally about the commitment.

related.reason: Both hand construction to AI so the graded work becomes defending the assumptions or claims the polished output depends on.
Both build a live artifact in minutes and grade the judgment about the numbers — sensitivity here, disconfirmation there — not the artifact.
